title: Second-survey heat gave no clear annual coral-cover link in four Atlantic and Pacific samples in 1998-2019
abstract: We tested heat stress at the second of two annual surveys against hard-coral cover change. HeatCRD version 1 gave 1,115 pairs at 428 sites in 31 countries. We matched site, source, depth and calendar month. Four Atlantic and Pacific period models controlled initial heat, initial cover, year, month and source. Slopes ranged from -1.09 to +0.37 cover percentage points per four TSA degree-heating weeks. All four corrected intervals included zero. Exact follow-up was available for only 3.5-7.8% of eligible baseline cells. Reef Check supplied 94.2% of pairs. Removing Reef Check gave a positive slope in the later Pacific sample and too few records in the other samples. These data did not establish a repeated heat link to annual cover change. Sparse follow-up, low heat support, source selection and survey-date heat limit inference. The result does not show that heat causes no coral loss. The package gives matched data, source hashes, code, uncertainty, a figure and independent checks.

display.caption: Left: heat slopes at the second survey with 98.75% site-cluster intervals. Right: complete pairs as a share of eligible baseline cells. Exact annual site, source, month and depth matching defines the sample.

citations.reason: Prior Reef Check archive test used heat at the first visit. We use HeatCRD and heat at both visits. The archives share records, so this is not independent validation.
